title: Upper resource/Voice teardown: concrete ordering and remaining lifetime boundaries

claims.title: Point-selected retirement
claims.finding: For nonzero address, the first list record with unsigned start=QWORD+1624 <= address < (start+zero-extended DWORD+1600) is selected. If supplied, the caller callback receives that record before a tail call12E460(record,0). This wrapper does not test ResourceEntry+1604 or wait for audio eligibility.
claims.limits: Intact list/readable records and no intervening mutation are premises. Addition is machine-width; no wrap validation.12E460 may invoke its own registered callback; NULL supplied callback does not suppress that separate callback. No global absence of external protection.

claims.title: Range-selected retirement
claims.finding: Repeatedly calls12E100(start,end), then12E460(record,flag), until lookup returns zero. There is no local ResourceEntry+1604 test in either this wrapper or12E460.
claims.limits: Termination depends on callbacks/destruction actually removing matching records and no external changes. No claim that arbitrary input addresses are safe.

claims.title: Exact range predicate
claims.finding: Uses exact endpoint equality or four strict endpoint-inside comparisons. Adjacent nonoverlapping normal intervals are rejected. An empty query point strictly inside a nonempty record can match; this is not interchangeable with a generic half-open interval-overlap utility.
claims.limits: Unsigned64 address arithmetic and zero-extended32 length. Boundary, degenerate and wrap examples are synthetic arithmetic tests, not evidence that runtime records assume those states.

claims.title: Zero-gated sweep differs from forced retirement
claims.finding: This separate list sweep skips a record when DWORD+1604 is nonzero. For zero it optionally invokes dispatch[index+1612].callback+24, unlinks from the global list, then invokes record virtual+0 with flags1.
claims.limits: The complete meaning and all writers of+1604 are not established here. It must not be called an audio lease/refcount merely because it gates this sweep. Virtual calls/callbacks may have further effects.

claims.title: Pre-copy Voice stop
claims.finding: For nonzero-size, nonalias BAR records, type34 dispatches1DE5C0 on the decoded wrapper pointer; types1/17/20/30/46 recurse. Type48 has no such case in the captured46-type map.1DE5C0 matches request+24 by exact pointer and request+53==6, calls1DE320, then for matching ORIGIN data invalidates group2 by DWORD+12.
claims.limits: No matching request means that helper does not reach its ORIGIN invalidation. Stop marks request+52=4; it neither proves synchronous backend quiescence nor establishes all callers/aliases.

claims.title: Post-copy Voice stop uses relocated pointer
claims.finding: Relocation first updates each nonzero-size BAR record pointer using the base delta. A nonalias type34 then passes the new decoded pointer to1DE5C0. It does not rebind old request+24 pointers. The same selected recursive types are present.
claims.limits: Pointer decoding validity, nested data bounds and external request management remain premises. Type48 is outside this46-case map. No safety claim for arbitrary BAR data.

claims.title: Local relocation order
claims.finding: On the selected existing-payload/nonzero-size path:3A62B0(oldBAR), optional matching ResourceEntry update(+16 and+1624) plus ReplaceEntry auxiliary+112 target+128 delta, direction-aware16-byte payload copies when old!=new,3A6120(newBAR),39E900. This supplies concrete pre-copy and post-copy type34 stop passes.
claims.limits: Refines prior relocation research; this body is a fresh recapture, not new coverage. Overlap/reload branches and callbacks differ. Aligned size/readable bounds, exact pointer matching and serialized use are required; no global safe hot-reload guarantee.

claims.title: Resource code retirement
claims.finding: Scans for DWORD+72==requested code. If flag DWORD+68 bit1 is clear, only byte+1==3 takes BAR release3A6A10(payload+88,1), then39E2A0 and manager virtual+16. Flag bit1 set takes unlink/free without that BAR release. The body has no WORD+2 counter gate.
claims.limits: Intact list and manager contract assumed. This is not a proof that callers legitimately pass a code while users still exist or that counter gating is absent elsewhere.

claims.title: Actor switch order is mode-dependent
claims.finding: Captures old Actor+2336 before the switch. Mode0 sets Actor+2488 bit0x10 and yields until3BFB70 says the old pointer is absent from the Actor list, then yields once with argument1. Mode1 instead calls descriptor virtual+328; other nonzero modes skip both local branches. The common suffix calls39D010(code),code+1,code+2 before3CD980(context,oldBuffer,...).
claims.limits: List absence is not an eternal no-reuse/ABA or audio-completion guarantee. Mode1 virtual target and caller mode invariants remain open. The old buffer is held as a raw register value across yields; no separate retain is visible in this body.

claims.title: Voice replacement before containing-resource retirement
claims.finding: Waits by yielding while global2A244D8 is nonzero, writes the supplied context there, clears a matching cache-used bit, calls3CDE50(newId,oldBuffer), then12EEA0(oldBuffer,NULL), then clears global2A244D8.
claims.limits: Plain loads/stores are not a demonstrated mutex or cross-thread exclusion. Normal call-return order only; no progress proof. The NULL caller callback still permits12E460 registered callbacks.

claims.title: Three searched cache rows and completion marker
claims.finding: For valid helper result and WORD+76 in1..15, searches three cache rows by two keys. A match marks used and returns. Otherwise selects the first clear used-bit among three rows, writes its keys, constructs the regional battle-voice path, requests loading via3A0B30 with3CDDF0 callback, sets context+24=1, and yields until that marker clears.
claims.limits: After all three searched rows are marked used and no key matches, the local index advances to3 and is used without a local rejection. Physical cache allocation, reserved fallback-row intent and live reachability are not established: no out-of-bounds/crash claim. Callback ordering relative to setting the wait marker is external.

claims.title: Callback bridge and marker-clear witness
claims.finding: With nonzero second argument,3CDDF0 forwards buffer,length,slot and3CE030 callback through1DF0E0, which selects type3 at1E03E0. With zero it clears current global context+24 directly.3CE030 also clears that field when the global is nonzero.
claims.limits: No full1E03E0/request lifecycle or completion guarantee is derived. The callback targets a global current context, without an identity check visible in these small bodies. ABI inferred from actual registers, not the decompiler int width for pointers.

claims.title: Group1 copy-mode handoff before range retirement
claims.finding: Calls1363B0(key,1),13B2E0(key,buffer,length,group1,mode0), then12EF30(buffer,buffer+signExtendedLength,0). It preserves registration return value but does not condition retirement on success.
claims.limits: Mode0 contract is prior work; current claim is call order and mode argument, not proof of native worker completion. Signed length can produce nonstandard ranges; only bounded synthetic arithmetic considered.

claims.title: Group2 ownership branches differ from borrowed voice
claims.finding: ORIGIN with nonzero payload+32 uses13B2E0(group2,mode0). SeBlock resolves a replacement, registers its+96 payload using mode0, then aligned-frees nonzero+96 and clears it, regardless of returned status. The ordinary branch chooses mode1 only for unsigned(key-20)<=1, otherwise mode0, then retires matching source ranges. This differs from1DFD70 ORIGIN voice mode2.
claims.limits: No general validity/size/allocator/asynchronous-safety proof. SeBlock lookup remains a dependency boundary. ORIGIN branch does not itself free wrapper+32. Native success/failure behavior was not exercised.

claims.title: Actor Voice stop precedes local resource decrements
claims.finding: Previously captured BTLNPC destructor4069C0 calls base Voice destructor3CD8E0 on Actor+3000 before3B3D60.3B3D60 calls3E61E0 on Actor+2320. That releases its nonnull+16/+24/+32 resource pointers through39DA10 then clears them. Voice destructor stops a nonzero handle via1DE500 and clears its handle before this resource step.
claims.limits: This composes direct local call order, assuming normal returns and the selected concrete destructor. Request marking/backend stopping is not BankEntry destruction; other actor types, bulk cleanup and callbacks remain outside this chain.

claims.title: Local resource counter decrement has no floor check
claims.finding: Finds the first resource record whose payload+88 equals the input, then adds0xffff to WORD+2. No local underflow guard. The no-match path retains RAX=0 and has the same WORD[RAX+2] add.
claims.limits: Only a body-local precondition: valid matching resource is required. No claim that the no-match path or counter wrap occurs in normal play. This resource-list WORD is distinct from audio-bank WORD+52 and ResourceEntry DWORD+1604.
